I computed the Q3 answers and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. I did **not** check the method against your Q2 reference values: the project's CLAUDE.md says not to compare results with example or reference values, so I submitted the first result as is.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment by net sales | consumer, 305,847,857 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 297 |
| c. Top category by net sales | acc, 257,906,791 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u132@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 286 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 678,850 |
| h. Sep vs. Aug growth in net sales | 37.6% |

How I applied the definitions:
- **Segment names:** The data has variants like `" consumer"`, `"Enterprise "` and `"SMB"`. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them, so they collapse into three segments: consumer, enterprise and smb.
- **Quarter:** All order times are stored in UTC (`...Z`), so I took orders placed from 2025-07-01 up to, but not including, 2025-10-01 by UTC date.
- **Rounding:** Line amounts and per-unit refunds are each rounded down to the won, as you specified. The growth rate uses exact decimal math, then rounds half up to one decimal place.
- **Average per order (g):** Total net sales divided by the number of paid orders that have line items, rounded down.

Because I skipped the Q2 check, I can't confirm the definitions were applied exactly as intended. Rerunning the same query on Q2 would tell you.
